# Design selection: work ID

- Canonical brief / RQ / delivery slice:
- Decision owner and source:
- Decision status: proposed / reviewed
- Effective rubric ID/version:
- Declared budget, actual use and remaining authorization:

## Retained candidates

| Candidate ID / revision or digest | Rubric version | Matching evaluation/evidence | Required failures or missing evidence | Required ratings | Eligible under this rubric? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | | | | | |

## Decision

- Selected candidate/revision, or none:
- Contract outcome: accepted / needs-work / unverified
- Rationale and alternatives, including earlier candidates:
- Stop reason: contract-satisfied / budget-exhausted / plateau / unresolved-decision
- Residual findings, human decisions and limitations:
- Required follow-up / owner / exact artifacts for next session:

Choose an earlier candidate when its matching evidence better meets the effective
contract. Never silently replace its revision or attach another candidate's report.
A material rubric change creates a new version: reevaluate retained candidates
before comparison under it. Old acceptance remains scoped to the old version.
Budget exhaustion or plateau grants no extra rounds and cannot make a failure pass.
If no candidate qualifies, retain needs-work/unverified and the next bounded action.

A human may choose to proceed with recorded risk; preserve the original check
results and missing evidence. Design selection never changes specification,
review, merge, CI or finish policy. Retain all candidate references and reports in
approved storage; do not delete authored artifacts while cleaning an iteration.
